dedupe_keys.name: ieee pes working group review benchmarking and validation of cascading failure analysis tools with a survey of test cases and historical outage data 2016

description: This paper by the IEEE Power and Energy Society working group on cascading failures reviews how cascading outage simulators and analysis tools can be verified, validated and benchmarked, and lists the test cases and historical data available for doing so. It appeared in IEEE Transactions on Power Systems in 2016. It argues that tools are hard to check against reality because historical cascades are rare and usually start from several combined outages, defines benchmarking as a systematic, reproducible validation procedure, describes a wide range of international public and non-public power system test cases with details on how to access them, and describes sources of historical outage and operations data for validation, ending with recommendations. Coverage is international, mainly North American and European systems. Format and access: the accepted manuscript PDF on a working group member's site. Licence: IEEE copyright, with academic content mining permitted; free to read. Caveats: some listed cases are not public, and links date from 2016. It is a starting point for calibrating and validating cascading failure and network flow models of power grids that feed other infrastructures. Related catalogue records are PGLib-OPF and the University of Washington Power Systems Test Case Archive.
